summary:
Abandoned but not Forgotten

Space science is often taught through dense texts, which makes it feel distant to young people. As a result, many lose interest in the machines that drove human progress, and in the people who built and operated them.

We want young people to appreciate both the machines and the people behind them. To do that, we created a fun animated video full of moving visuals, in which three NASA machines, Curiosity rover, IBEX, and Ulysses, tell their own stories. Each story explains why the machine was sent, how it worked, and what it discovered.

 The language is simple and the visuals are lively, so even viewers with no interest in space can follow along.

Target audience: ages 10-14

Sources: NASA Science (Curiosity, IBEX, Ulysses). All facts will be checked against NASA sources.
details:
Our project is a short animated video for ages 10-14 that tells the stories of three NASA machines, the Curiosity rover, IBEX, and Ulysses, each in its own voice. Every story explains why the machine was sent to space, how it worked, and what it discovered, so viewers appreciate the people behind the machines as well as the machines itself.

Instead of listing technical facts, each machine acts as a narrator and takes the viewer through its own journey in a cinematic style, with lively moving visuals and simple language. The video opens with a short introduction, then presents each machine's story, and ends with a conclusion that connects the three machines: Curiosity on the surface of Mars, and IBEX and Ulysses studying the Sun and the boundary of its influence. Subtitles are included for accessibility. All facts are checked against NASA sources.

The project makes space science easier and more exciting for young people, including those with no prior interest in space. It helps them appreciate the machines that drove human progress, and the people who built them, even when those machines have finished their missions or are far from Earth and rarely remembered.

Goals:

Replace dry, text-heavy space education with an engaging story.

Teach the purpose, design, and achievements of each machine in simple language.

Inspire young viewers to value space exploration and the people behind it.

Tools used:

Canva, Cupcut, ibis paint, Background eraser, Alight motion and ElevenLabs.
